title: Additive localized cocycle comparison and its concrete chain maps
statement: Let C, R and the chosen derived slice categories satisfy [def-per-local-rhom-normalization-interface]. Let L,I be complexes of sheaves of R-modules, U an object and n an integer. The cycles in the sections at U of Hom(L,I) are additively equivalent to degree n cocycles between their restrictions, with component the fixed product projection. Their homology is additively equivalent to homotopy-category morphisms from the restriction of L to the shifted restriction of I, sending a cycle class to its chain map. If I is K-injective, the same holds in the derived slice category. A sheaf cycle determines a concrete local chain map into the restriction of I[n], with exactly those components.

proof.text: Apply the degreewise additive cochain comparison and its differential compatibility to construct an isomorphism from the section Hom complex to the external Hom complex. The induced cycles and homology isomorphisms, followed by Mathlib HomComplex.leftHomologyData and CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv, give additive equivalences and the projection and cycle-class formulas. Exact slice restriction preserves K-injectivity. The fully faithful localization into a K-injective target gives an additive equivalence of homotopy and derived Hom groups; quotientCompQhIso naturality identifies its cycle-class map with Q applied to the chain map. For a sheaf cycle, evaluate its inclusion: iCycles_d makes the resulting element lie in the kernel of the differential of the sections complex. The concrete kernel description constructs sectionCycle without any exactness assumption on taking sections. Reindex the canonical external cocycle and compose with the inverse restriction-shift comparison to construct its local chain map. The mapHomologicalComplex shift component is the identity, giving the prescribed component formula. The component formula determines the cycle equivalence uniquely by extensionality. Surjectivity of the homology projection makes its class formula determine the cohomology equivalence uniquely. Thus all choices used to construct the public equivalences are fixed by the equations used downstream.
